 ORDER

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.57/2024, registered at Police Station-Gandhinagar, District Bhopal (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 420, 467, 468, 120-B and 409 of Indian Penal Code and under Sections 7, 13(1)(a) and 13(2) of Anti Corruption Act, 1988.
2. Learned senior counsel appearing for the applicant submitted that no forged document has been prepared by applicant neither any criminal breach of trust has been committed.
Other offences are punishable less than seven years of imprisonment.

As per prosecution case, husband of applicant has transferred amount of Rs.2 crore in account of Kumar Mayank and out of which a DD of Rs.19 lacs was prepared from his account to account of applicant Seema Verma.

It is submitted that Smt. Seema Verma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20438947/
1 applicant does not have any role.

sentences.text: She is a passive accused in the case.
In these circumstances, he prayed that applicant may be released on bail.
3 . Learned Government Advocate appearing for State opposed the application for grant of bail.

It is submitted that applicant had knowledge that she had received Rs.19 lacs in her account and later on,
she has also prepared a FDR from said amount.
Therefore, knowledge on part of applicant is gathered.
Applicant is equally responsible for the offence.
I n these circumstances, applicant may not be released on bail.

4. Heard the counsel for the parties.
5. Applicant does not have any role in cheating and defalcation.
No forged document is prepared by her neither criminal breach of trust has been committed.
Applicant is a passive accused in the case since amount has been credited in her account.
Applicant is a woman.
6. Considering aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, bail application filed by applicant is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for her regular appearance before Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of trial on aforesaid conditions.

(VISHAL DHAGAT) JUDGE sp/-
